problem: The chapter fixes one convention (z_t near 1 means the candidate is used, z_t near 0 keeps the old state), but many standard implementations, including PyTorch's GRU, use the opposite sign: h_t = (1 − z_t)⊙h~_t + z_t⊙h_{t-1}. A student who checks code after reading this will think the chapter is wrong.
fix: Add one line after the GRU equations: 'Textbooks and libraries differ on which side z_t weights. This book uses z_t⊙h~_t + (1 − z_t)⊙h_{t-1}. Always read the formula attached to the code you use.'

problem: Saying peepholes let 'the gates see c_{t-1} directly' is only right for the forget and input gates. The peephole into the output gate uses the freshly updated cell state c_t, because h_t is formed after c_t exists.
fix: Write: 'Peephole connections feed c_{t-1} into the forget and input gates, and the new c_t into the output gate.'

fix: Tag each equation as its own [formula] line and give its terms right after it, or at least put the cell update c_t = f_t ⊙ c_{t-1} + i_t ⊙ c~_t on its own tagged line since the worked example depends on it.
